mappings.note: Defines reproduction then, for the marks, the importance of DNA copying - the heredity mechanism, C 3.3. LO-1 rejected: no sexual-vs-asexual variation claim.
Defines variation and asks why it benefits a species - the variation half of C 3.3, without the mode comparison that C 3.3-LO-1 requires.
DNA as the information source for proteins and DNA copying as the basic event of reproduction - C 3.3 heredity mechanism.
One bacterial and one viral STD plus prevention - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5.
Roles of seminal vesicles and prostate plus two functions of the testes - parts and functions of the human male tract, C 4.2-LO-4.
Names the animal gametes, defines fertilisation and locates it in the human female - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.

Part one asks the two types of reproduction (C 3.2-LO-6); part two asks WHICH confers new characteristics and HOW, answerable only by the greater variation of sexual reproduction (C 3.3-LO-1). Both are needed.
Definition and diagram of binary fission in Amoeba - fission is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Defines regeneration and explains why complex organisms cannot use it - an asexual mode and its limits, C 3.2-LO-6.
Stages of binary fission in Amoeba - fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Two functions of the copper-T - a contraceptive device, C 4.2-LO-5. Not LO-4: the uterus is only the site, not the subject.
Regeneration distinguished from reproduction, plus the mode of asexual reproduction in Plasmodium - both asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.
Rhizopus multiplying by spores, with a diagram - an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6. Not LO-7: Rhizopus is a fungus, not a flowering plant.
Reproductive parts of a flower and unisexual vs bisexual flowers - flower structure inside C 3.2-LO-7. (Stored concept tag 'Reproductive Health and Contraception' is wrong.)

Human sperm vs ovum (size, motility, food store) and why the difference matters - the structure/function of what the testis and ovary produce, C 4.2-LO-4. Not C 3.3, which would be the chromosome angle, and that is not asked.
Spirogyra fragmenting and Planaria regenerating - both asexual modes named or implied by C 3.2-LO-6.
Definition of STDs and the one that destroys immunity (AIDS) - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5. (Stored concept tag 'Human Male Reproductive System' is wrong.)
Sites blocked in vasectomy/tubectomy and reasons for using contraceptives - surgical family planning, C 4.2-LO-5. The organs are named only as the sites of the method, so LO-4 is not the demand.
Vegetative propagation defined with two advantages - named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6.
Type of asexual reproduction in Planaria, Rhizopus, Spirogyra and Hydra - four asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.
Part (a) asexual vs sexual reproduction (C 3.2-LO-6); part (b) self vs cross pollination, which is inside the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7. Neither outcome covers the other half.
Two points on the importance of DNA copying - heredity mechanism, C 3.3, not the sexual-vs-asexual variation claim of LO-1.
Budding vs spore formation - two asexual modes, budding named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Which listed plants propagate vegetatively, plus one advantage - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6.
Illustrating regeneration in Planaria - an asexual mode, C 3.2-LO-6.
Bryophyllum leaves sprout plantlets from notch buds - vegetative propagation, C 3.2-LO-6. (Stored concept tag 'Pollination and Fertilisation (Plants)' is wrong: no pollen is involved.)
Why the testes hang in the scrotum (lower temperature for sperm formation) - the function of a named male part, C 4.2-LO-4.

Three separate demands: post-fertilisation fate of ovary and ovule in angiosperms (C 3.2-LO-7), two asexually reproducing animals (C 3.2-LO-6), and the human gonads (C 4.2-LO-4). Each part carries marks and no single outcome covers the other two.
Judging binary against multiple fission - two asexual modes weighed against each other, C 3.2-LO-6.

Chromosome numbers in egg nucleus, zygote, endosperm and leaf cell of tobacco - haploid/diploid/triploid arithmetic, C 3.3. Not LO-7: nothing about pollination or seed development is asked, only the counts.
Why asexual offspring are clones AND the advantage of sexual reproduction - both halves rest on sexual reproduction generating variation that asexual does not, C 3.3-LO-1.
Part (a) the uterus as the site of implantation and development (C 4.2-LO-4); part (b) the advantages of mechanical barriers, which is contraception and infection protection (C 4.2-LO-5).
Bryophyllum vs Jasmine leaves, then asexual vs sexual differences - vegetative propagation and the mode distinction, both in C 3.2-LO-6.
Which flower parts ripen into fruit and seed, plus labelling - the fertilisation-to-seed end of C 3.2-LO-7.
Regeneration in Planaria and why it is not universal - an asexual mode and its limits, C 3.2-LO-6.
Seed germination. C 3.2-LO-7 stops at seed formation, so germination reaches NO outcome in this frame; C 3.2 is the most specific true code.
Sex hormones of the testis and ovary with one function each - the endocrine function of named reproductive organs, C 4.2-LO-4.
Part (a) pollination vs fertilisation (C 3.2-LO-7); part (b) mode of reproduction in earthworm, frog, Rhizopus and Plasmodium, which spans sexual and asexual modes (C 3.2-LO-6).
Why prenatal sex determination is banned - reproductive health at the social level, C 4.2-LO-5.
Placenta and two of its roles - a pregnancy structure and its function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Comparing vegetative propagation in Bryophyllum (leaf buds) and money plant (stem cuttings) - C 3.2-LO-6.
Three demands: where a flower's male and female germ cells form (C 3.2-LO-7), the significance of variation (C 3.3), and the principle of regeneration (C 3.2-LO-6). All three carry marks separately.
Two bacterial STDs and how oral pills prevent pregnancy - reproductive health plus a contraceptive method, both C 4.2-LO-5.
The ovary working both as a gamete-producing organ and as an endocrine gland - a single part with two functions, C 4.2-LO-4.
DNA in the nucleus as the protein-making information source and the basic events of reproduction - C 3.3 heredity mechanism.
Why budding, fragmentation and regeneration are asexual, plus which organism uses spore formation - budding and fragmentation are named in C 3.2-LO-6.
Diagrams of spore formation in Rhizopus and regeneration in Planaria - two asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.
Why multicellular organisms cannot simply 'divide cell by cell' - specialised tissues rule out fission, which is the mode distinction of C 3.2-LO-6.
Naming pollination, its external agents and its two types - the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Placenta as the nourishing organ and the cause of parturition - functions of pregnancy structures, C 4.2-LO-4.
Modes of pollination defined - the first step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Unisexual vs bisexual flowers and which listed plants are unisexual - flower structure in C 3.2-LO-7.
Events in binary fission in Amoeba and which organisms regenerate - fission and regeneration, C 3.2-LO-6.
Which organ implants the zygote and what the fallopian tubes do - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Vas deferens (testis to urethra) and oviduct (ovary to uterus) - part-and-function in both human tracts, C 4.2-LO-4.
Part (a) the advantage of sexual over asexual reproduction, which is variation (C 3.3-LO-1); part (b) the male and female parts of a flower (C 3.2-LO-7).
Reproduction vs regeneration, and organisms that regenerate - an asexual mode and its boundary, C 3.2-LO-6.
What pollination is and how it happens - the opening step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Binary fission in Amoeba (any plane) vs Leishmania (fixed plane) - fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Which human organs are the site of fertilisation and the producer of ova - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Which organs implant the zygote and admit the sperm - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Radicle vs plumule - seedling anatomy after germination. C 3.2-LO-7 runs only to seed formation, so no outcome reaches this; the competency C 3.2 is the honest level.
Pollen grain vs ovule - the male and female units of the C 3.2-LO-7 sequence.
Why chromosome number stays the same across sexually reproducing generations - meiosis then fertilisation, a chromosome mechanism (C 3.3), not the variation comparison of LO-1.
Path of sperm to the exterior and the functions of prostate and seminal-vesicle secretions - part-and-function of the male tract, C 4.2-LO-4.
Four methods of asexual reproduction other than fission - the enumeration in C 3.2-LO-6.
Slide-based item on the stages of budding in yeast; budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6. Flagged: the stem carries only the instruction and no actual question.

The whole demand is the correct order of microscope steps (mount, mirror/diaphragm, low power, high power). Neither C 3.2 nor C 3.3 nor C 4.2 covers laboratory technique, and this chapter's frame carries no scientific-inquiry competency, so the goal CG 3 'explores the structure and function of the living world at the cellular level' is the only honest code.
Difference between the nucleus in Amoeba's binary fission and in yeast budding - two asexual modes compared, C 3.2-LO-6.
The asexual mode in which the parent's identity is lost in two offspring (binary fission), with the starting event - fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
What a student should report on seeing a slide of binary fission in Amoeba - the observable stages of fission, C 3.2-LO-6. Unlike qid:86266, the answer is the biology, not the instrument.
What budding means, with an example - budding is named in C 3.2-LO-6.
'What does the diagram given here correctly illustrate?' with no figure supplied; nothing specific can be verified, so only the competency C 3.2 is honestly claimable. Flagged as figure-dependent.
Two tabulated differences between binary and multiple fission - fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Same demand as qid:86268 - the asexual mode where the parent's identity is lost, i.e. binary fission, C 3.2-LO-6.
Naming and drawing the sequence of asexual reproduction in yeast (budding) - C 3.2-LO-6.
Defines fertilisation, implantation, placenta, gestation, parturition, ovulation - all events located in named human reproductive structures, C 4.2-LO-4.
Explains 'fission' and 'regeneration' - two asexual modes, C 3.2-LO-6.
Pollination, its two types and their difference - the pollination step of C 3.2-LO-7.
Vegetative propagation, when it is used and three of its methods - named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6.
Fertilisation defined, external vs internal, and its site in humans (fallopian tube) - the function of the human oviduct, C 4.2-LO-4. Not LO-7: the worked case is human.
Unisexual and bisexual defined with an example each - flower types inside C 3.2-LO-7. Not C 4.2-LO-4: the examples are flowers.
Double fertilisation in plants - the fertilisation step of C 3.2-LO-7, including endosperm formation.
Binary fission in Amoeba and a Bryophyllum leaf with buds - fission and vegetative propagation, both in C 3.2-LO-6.
Implantation, placenta and the duration of human pregnancy - functions of the human uterus, C 4.2-LO-4.
Defines STDs, names four and identifies AIDS as the immune-destroying one - reproductive health, C 4.2-LO-5.
Three differences between pollination and fertilisation - the two named steps of C 3.2-LO-7.
DNA expanded, located and its role in cell reproduction explained - the heredity mechanism of C 3.3. Not C 3.3-LO-1: no sexual-vs-asexual variation claim.
Vegetative propagation explained with two examples and two advantages - named verbatim in C 3.2-LO-6.
Asexual method used by rose, yeast and Planaria, plus what fragmentation is - fragmentation and budding are named in C 3.2-LO-6.
How many eggs a month, where fertilisation occurs, and the fate of an unfertilised egg - ovary/oviduct/uterus function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Labelling a male-system diagram, naming the hormone from the testis and the contents of the two tubes - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.

Part (a) asexual vs sexual reproduction (C 3.2-LO-6) and part (c) pollination vs fertilisation (C 3.2-LO-7). Part (b) plumule vs radicle is post-germination and reaches no outcome; it is subsumed by the shared parent C 3.2, so no third code is added.
Part (a) why vegetative propagation is practised (C 3.2-LO-6); parts (b) and (c) the flower parts carrying germ cells and the agents of pollination (C 3.2-LO-7).
Self vs cross pollination and the fate of pollen on a compatible stigma - pollination into fertilisation, C 3.2-LO-7.
'Name the parts A, B and C and state one function of each' with no figure supplied; the subject cannot be determined, so only the competency C 3.2 is honest. Flagged as figure-dependent.
One function each of vas deferens, testis and prostate gland - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.

Part (a) names the organism whose binary fission has a fixed orientation (Leishmania) - fission, C 3.2-LO-6. Part (b) labels a germinating seed, which reaches no outcome here (C 3.2-LO-7 ends at seed formation), so no second code is added.
Names parts 1-5 of the female system and the site of fertilisation - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
How oral pills act as contraceptives and why they can harm - a hormonal family-planning method and its health cost, C 4.2-LO-5.
Labels the ovum-secreting part and the implantation site, and asks the consequence of a blocked fallopian tube - part-and-function, C 4.2-LO-4.
Function of ovary, fallopian tube and uterus - the exact demand of C 4.2-LO-4.

Part (a) names a unisexual flower (C 3.2-LO-7); part (b) the birth canal, i.e. the vagina (C 4.2-LO-4). Part (c) on the factors setting population size reaches no outcome in this frame and is left uncoded rather than forced onto C 4.2-LO-5.
Barrier, hormonal and surgical contraception each explained with an example - methods of family planning, C 4.2-LO-5.
